[mathematical] Inverse formulation of Fidelity (Equation 1)
In Section III.A.1, Equation 1 places the error term $\|f(x_i) - g(x_i)\|^2$ in the denominator. If the explanation model perfectly mimics the underlying model, the denominator approaches 0, causing the fidelity score to approach infinity. However, Section V explicitly states: "A lower fidelity score (closer to 0) indicates that the explanation model accurately represents the predictions of the original model". The formula directly contradicts the intended scale and mathematically explodes on perfect fits.
*Fix:* Invert the fraction to compute the error ratio correctly, for example: $\frac{\|f(x_i) - g(x_i)\|^2}{\|f(x_i)\|^2}$.
